content:
Hector B. (Finance): quick pulse check - ReckonWare vs Ledgerly vs InvoiceSmith. CFO asked for "negotiation anchors" (aka what to push on) + an ask list for sales before we move to exec approval. Can procurement take lead?
Nora P. (Procurement): I'll lead. High-level ask list: 1) Clarify true unit pricing (processing vs line-item), 2) Pilot credits, 3) Commit tiers & opt-out terms, 4) Migration support credits, 5) Export / egress fees, 6) SLA credits for parser regressions. Anything else?
Samir D. (EngOps): add connector commitments: guaranteed Snowflake/S3 ingest timelines, webhook concurrency limits, and support for incremental reprocessing without recharging us. Also ask for API rate limits and burst behavior.
Olivia R. (Legal): add data residency / subprocessor list, DPA sample, indemnity caps, and termination data return timeline. If vendor wants a minimum processing commit, flag that as a showstopper unless there9s a strong discount.
Jules (ReckonWare Sales): happy to answer. ReckonWare pricing: $0.035 per processed invoice line by default; enterprise tiers reduce to $0.022 at >1M lines/mo. We provide a 60-day pilot with $5k credit. No mandatory commit if pilot accepted. SOC2 + subprocessor list available.
vendor-bot: "ReckonWare SOC2 link shared with procurement@redwood.com"
Hector B. (Finance): good. For modeling, please provide 1-year TCO at current volume (~300k invoices / 2.1M lines) and a 3-year forecast with a baseline 10% annual growth. Include migration amortized at $20k one-time.
Nora P. (Procurement): will do. Quick question: how strong is our leverage? Any comparable vendors we can reference for pricing?
Samir D. (EngOps): Ledgerly mentioned a 6mo onboarding minimum and a lower per-line price but charges for schema changes. InvoiceSmith offers pay-as-you-go but has higher egress fees. Those are our levers: commit length vs price, and migration credits.
Jules (ReckonWare Sales): we can consider a 12-month committed discount (15%) in exchange for a 6-month minimum. Also can include one week of professional services for mapping during onboarding.
Olivia R. (Legal): that 6-month minimum needs a clear exit for material breach or repeated SLA misses. Also, renegotiation clause on price increases.
Hector B. (Finance): include run-rate sensitivity table (if volume 20% up/down). Also add column for manual-review overhead (ops FTE hours/week if parser accuracy drops).
Nora P. (Procurement): action items: 1) I'll ask all three vendors for a detailed rate card (unit breakout, egress, export, retention tiers) and pilot terms by EOD tomorrow. 2) Samir provide integration estimates (eng-weeks) for each vendor. 3) Olivia list top 5 legal redlines to push back. We'll reconvene Thurs AM to finalize negotiation strategy.
Samir D. (EngOps): will estimate: ReckonWare = 4 engineer-days (Snowflake + mapping), Ledgerly = 2 engineer-weeks (custom mapping UI), InvoiceSmith = 1 engineer-week + SRE validation. I'll also ask Ledgerly if schema-change fees are real.
Jules (ReckonWare Sales): sending detailed rate card now; can also do a quick demo for execs if helpful.
vendor-bot: "ReckonWare rate card uploaded to procurement drive: https://drive.example/reckon-ratecard.pdf"
Olivia R. (Legal): procurement pls cc legal on vendor answers. I9ll draft protective language for commit clauses and SLA credits.
Hector B. (Finance): priority: we need a recommendation memo by next Monday. If procurement can get pilot credits + PS hours that will hugely impact the TCO favorably. Thanks all.
Nora P. (Procurement): noted 44d3fb. I'll start outreach now and post updates here.
